articles.title: Police arrest 15-year-old boy in Tallahassee mass shooting that left 11 injured
articles.summary: The Tallahassee Police Department arrested a 15-year-old boy in connection with the Oct. 24 mass shooting that left 11 people injured outside Bragg Stadium after Florida A&M University's homecoming football game. Anthony Rivers III was arrested Sunday, Oct. 25 in the mass shooting, which was one of the worst in Tallahassee history. Rivers was arrested on 11 counts of attempted homicide and one count of possession of a firearm by a delinquent, said Alicia Hill, a TPD spokeswoman. The Tallahassee Democrat names minors when they are charged with violent offenses. "Our investigation indicates that a physical altercation occurred before shots were fired," TPD Police Chief Lawrence Revell said in a hastily arranged Oct. 26 press conference. "At this stage of the investigation, none of the victims appear to have been the intended targets." Detectives believe the incident stemmed from a dispute between individuals known to one another. While at an earlier press conference hours after the shooting Revell said detective believed there was only a single shooter, he said additional arrests are possible. At least 12 people were injured, including 11 who were shot. Six of the victims were children, including the youngest victim who is 11, according to TPD Chief Lawrence Revell. A grandmother of one of the victims was also injured in the ensuing panic. Six of the victims were male and six were female. Six victims remain hospitalized, with one of the victims in critical condition. “What should have been a weekend of celebration in our community instead became a night of fear and violence for the victims and their families,” Revell said. “While this arrest marks a significant step forward, our work is far from over. We remain committed to holding those responsible accountable and getting answers for every family impacted by this tragedy.” TPD said its officers and investigators worked "around the clock" to identify the alleged shooter. "In the moments immediately following the shooting, our officers rushed toward danger to render aid to victims even before the scene was fully secured," Revell said. "I could not be prouder of the men and women of this department." Police said a "significant influx" of information poured in from the community. Before the arrest, TPD asked the public for any cellphone video or tips from witnesses. "Tips and digital evidence provided by members of the public have been vital to investigative efforts," he said. "But we are not finished." The investigation remains open and active. "This arrest represents progress, but we will not stop working until we fully establish what happened, identify everyone involved and bring the people to justice," he said. "Twelve people were injured Saturday night, twelve families had to confront something no family should have to face," he continued. "We owe those victims, their families and this community answers." TPD asks community for help To aid in this ongoing investigation, TPD has established a dedicated tip hotline (850-891-4610) and activated an evidence submission https://tallahasseepd.evidence.com/axon/community-request/public/perrystreetincident and is encouraging members of the public to securely share photos, videos and other information that may assist detectives. TPD encourages anyone who witnessed the incident or has information that may assist detectives to contact the Perry Street shooting hotline at 850-891-4610 or remain anonymous by calling Crime Solvers at 850-574-TIPS. "We need our community's help. No detail is too small, and no piece of information should go unreported," Revell said earlier. "If you know something, please share it with our detectives. Your information could be the key to holding those responsible accountable." Check back with Tallahassee.com for more on this story. Contact Jeff Burlew at jburlew@tallahassee.com or 850-599-2180. articles.title: U.S. military ready to strike Iran within 96 hours if Trump gives the order
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump shakes hands with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth in Sparrows Point, Maryland, on October 6. - Jim Watson/AFP/Getty Images US forces in the Middle East are prepared to launch new, potentially major, military operations against Iran “within 96 hours of receiving” an order from President Donald Trump, according to two US officials. Sufficient forces are now deployed in the region to carry out the potential attacks, the sources said. The scope of new US military operations would likely go beyond efforts to simply “mow the lawn” or maintain the status quo by striking radars, launchers and other Iranian assets that can be quickly reconstituted — as has been the case since Trump halted full combat operations earlier this year, the sources added. “It will be a big effort,” one of the officials told CNN. That view has been echoed by other current and former US officials familiar with internal military planning discussions — some of whom say it is a question of when, not if, Trump will issue a go-order. They believe it could come any time before the end of the year, though most likely after the US midterm elections. US officials acknowledge challenges, cite potential threat Iranian forces are now more familiar with US tactics, and it would therefore be harder for the American military to effectively destroy all potential intended targets. However, leaders in US Central Command and the Pentagon have been developing a wide-ranging target list, which includes Iranian energy infrastructure, military sites and nuclear facilities. Officials say that Trump has not made up his mind on what he will do after the midterms but that he appears to be leaning toward ordering major action. But officials also caution that Trump has appeared in the past to lean toward certain actions only to back off at the last moment. The White House declined to comment. A senior Pentagon official told CNN in a statement, “The Department is a planning organization, and its job is to develop and execute military options ordered by the President.” Recent US intelligence assessments indicate Iran and Houthi rebels are taking the possibility of renewed attacks by the US and potentially Israel very seriously, according to two additional sources familiar with the matter. If the US and Israel launch new military operations against Iran, Tehran and the Houthis would likely retaliate immediately by targeting American personnel and facilities around the region — and potentially beyond, the sources familiar with those recent US intelligence assessments said. An unclassified October 23 memo from Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton to Secretary of State Marco Rubio says US intelligence has found that “Iran has substantially increased efforts to target US personnel” and plotting efforts “have reached advanced stages in both the Middle East and certain other countries,” CNN previously reported . US intelligence officials believe Iran and the Houthis are unlikely to carry out preemptive escalatory attacks against American personnel or Israel at this point but would not hesitate to respond if Iran is targeted first by US or Israeli forces, one of the sources familiar with the latest American intelligence assessments noted. The Iranian national flag is seen in southern Tehran on September 18. - Morteza Nikoubazl/NurPhoto/AP/File But the regional threat posed by Iran and the Houthis is one reason why the US is expected to continue quietly pulling personnel from its embassies across the Middle East in the coming days, the source said. While the US Embassy in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, is the only American diplomatic facility in the region under ordered departure , one of the sources told CNN that others are expected to receive similar directives and those that do not will be scaled down under a personnel cap. Additionally, nonessential US military personnel who were expected to deploy to the Middle East as part of the next troop rotation have been told they are no longer being sent, according to a US official, underscoring the possibility of looming regional escalation. Adm. Brad Cooper, the CENTCOM commander, visited the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday as the US military maintains its blockade on Iranian ports and assists shipping traffic through the critical waterway. Cooper “observed the current operational environment” while flying over the strait in a helicopter, CENTCOM said, adding that he met with service members who cleared the waterway of Iranian mines. “We continue to stand shoulder to shoulder with our Gulf partners and the shipping industry,” Cooper said in a news release. “This visit underscores our strong commitment to continued freedom of navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.” Despite the increase in tankers transiting the strait, oil prices remain high, partly due to the threat of possible Iranian attacks. One US official acknowledged the status quo around the strait is “untenable” for the long term, and barring a last-minute diplomatic breakthrough, is one reason Trump may turn to military action — despite questions about whether the White House has a broader strategy for ending the conflict. Israel pushing for more strikes Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has been pushing to carry out new attacks against Iran, but US officials have requested he delay until the Trump administration is ready to conduct joint operations, according to two US officials and an Israeli security source. “Netanyahu really wanted and tried to convince Trump for a joint attack in Iran before the elections, and Trump did not give a green light,” the Israeli security source told CNN. The prime minister’s office said this was “fake news.” One reason Trump declined is because Israel Defense Forces chief of staff Eyal Zamir told US Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs, that it would harm the elections in Israel and lead to their postponement, the Israeli security source added. Israel’s Channel 12 News reported Sunday there was an “unprecedented” confrontation between Zamir and Netanyahu fewer than 48 hours before Tuesday’s vote. According to the report, Zamir received a directive from the political echelon related to Iran but requested an in-depth discussion and legal authorizations before carrying it out, fearing the action could lead to a miscalculation that could trigger an immediate conflict. Defense Minister Israel Katz said the report was “completely baseless and false.” Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks to his supporters on October 22 ahead of Israel's legislative election. - Jack Guez/AFP/Getty Images Israel was preparing for the possibility of launching additional attacks against Iran in the last week or so and had been lobbying US officials to support and complement those new strikes, a third source briefed on the matter told CNN. But senior US officials — including Trump — told Israel to hold off, instead signaling the two countries would launch joint operations soon. Israel appears to have delayed plans in the immediate term for additional strikes but is building up for potential joint operations with the US — likely after the American midterm elections, all of the sources said. Israel seemed to agree to delaying new strikes on Iran in part because it needs US support for missile defense, the source briefed on the matter added. Iran and the Houthis would likely retaliate against an attack and Israel’s defensive munitions have been strained during the war. Recent US intelligence assessments indicate that Netanyahu and his allies still lack a clear strategic objective beyond demonstrating some sort of “progress” and continuing to degrade the Iranian regime, one of the sources familiar with the reports added. Netanyahu said this week in a speech at an IDF graduation ceremony that his directive to the IDF, the Mossad and other security branches is to topple the regime in Iran. “The plans are ready, waiting for Trump’s approval, could be after the midterms,” the same source told CNN. This story has been updated with additional developments Monday. CNN’s Kevin Liptak contributed to this report. articles.title: What's at stake as Israel holds its most important election in years
articles.summary: Getty Images When Israelis go the polls on October 27, they will face a familiar question: Should Benjamin Netanyahu, the country’s longest-serving prime minister, stay in power? Nearly every recent election has been a referendum on Netanyahu. This time, many Israelis say the choice is more consequential than ever: not only about who will lead the country, but about where it is heading. It is the first national vote since the Hamas-led attack of October 7, 2023, the deadliest security failure in Israel’s history, and the wars that followed in Gaza, Lebanon and Iran, which have mobilized much of the country and subsequently deepened Israel’s international isolation. For many voters, this is the first chance to pass judgment on the leadership that presided over October 7 failures, to decide who should lead the country in conflict and who should carry the burden of increased military service. Netanyahu’s outgoing government – the first in decades to conclude a full four-year term – relied on far-right and ultra-Orthodox partners, who pushed Israel in a more nationalist and religious direction than ever before. He became the first sitting Israeli prime minister to stand trial on corruption charges as his government pursued a judicial overhaul aimed at weakening the supreme court and other checks on power. The overhaul effort sparked massive protests in 2023. At stake in Tuesday’s election is whether Israel keeps moving in the nationalistic, conservative and religious direction – or changes course. The answer might not be clear for weeks, because of the way Israeli coalitions are built. Polls suggest neither Netanyahu’s bloc nor the opposition is likely to win a majority alone, meaning the vote may launch Israel’s next political crisis rather than settle it. Who is running and who is ahead? Israelis vote for party lists, not individual candidates. In a society divided by nationality, religion, ethnicity and ideology, that produces a crowded field. Dozens of lists register each cycle, but only those that pass a 3.25% vote threshold win seats and enter the 120-seat Knesset, Israel’s parliament. On Monday, 36 parties were in play. Polls suggest 11 to 13 parties will meet the bar; seats are allocated through a proportional representation system. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu speaks to local residents and supporters during a campaign stop at HaTikva Market in Tel Aviv on Thursday. - Erik Marmor/Getty Images The two largest parties are Netanyahu’s right-wing Likud and Yashar, a new centrist party led by Gadi Eisenkot, a former military chief of staff who has emerged as his principal challenger. The latest Channel 12 opinion poll puts Eisenkot first with 23 seats, ahead of the Likud with 21, though other pollsters differ. On the pro-Netanyahu Channel 14, Likud is projected to take 30 seats and Eisenkot about 20. In head-to-head matchups about who is better suited to be prime minister, Eisenkot has led Netanyahu by a steady margin. But coming out as the largest party is not enough to win. A prime minister needs 61 seats to form a government, and no party has ever won that majority alone. So, election night usually settles very little. The real contest is the coalition calculus that follows, which can take days, weeks, and even months. Most polls put Netanyahu’s bloc, made up of Likud, two far-right parties led by Bezalel Smotrich and Itamar Ben-Gvir, and two ultra-Orthodox parties, at 49 to 55 seats, short of the 61-seat majority. The opposition, which looks strong on paper, is deeply fragmented: Eisenkot has parties led by former Prime Minister Naftali Bennett and former Defense Minister Avigdor Liberman to his right, and the Democrats party led by Yair Golan on his left. Bennett and Liberman have not endorsed Eisenkot and both have their own premiership aspirations. Leader of the Yashar party Gadi Eisenkot visits the Western Wall in Jerusalem's Old City on Thursday. - Mahmoud Illean/AP According to the opinion polls, any alternative government would probably need the support or the abstention of the Arab parties, and several opposition leaders have ruled out any cooperation. With no side holding a clear majority, a deadlock, a minority government, a unity government – or another election – are all plausible outcomes. What could swing the result? With neither bloc projected to win comfortably, the outcome may hinge on the margins: which small parties clear the 3.25% threshold and how many votes go to parties that miss it, effectively sending them down the drain. Turnout matters, since a few thousand votes can determine whether a party disappears entirely or enters parliament, or even becomes the kingmaker that breaks the deadlock between the blocs and reshapes the political map. Arab voter turnout could be pivotal. Palestinian citizens of Israel – who make up roughly 20% of the Israeli population – have traditionally voted at lower rates than the national average. In the 2022 election, the Arab turnout was 53.2%, while the general turnout was 70.6%. This time, pollsters expect it to exceed 60%. That would raise the threshold and make it harder for small parties to survive. Mansour Abbas, head of Israel's conservative Islamic Ra'am party, speaks at a campaign rally in the Arab-Israeli village of Abu Gosh on Wednesday. - Ahmad Gharabli/AFP/Getty Images Netanyahu’s coalition has several small parties at potential risk, including Smotrich’s Religious Zionism and a new right- wing party led by Ofer Winter, a prominent retired military general. While most opposition parties sit safely above the line, another new, uncommitted small party, connecting a reservist and economic agenda, is polling close to the 3.25% threshold. Another factor drawing attention is Israelis living abroad. Israel does not allow overseas voting, except for diplomatic staff, and official data suggests more than 11% of the 7.3 million eligible voters, about 810,000 people, live outside the country. Thousands plan to fly to Israel to vote in person, a number that could potentially impact the election. What do Israelis vote about? In a country that has been through years of war, security and accountability are powerful electoral forces. But opinion polls suggest the cost of living is also a leading concern for many voters – particularly for younger ones. According to the latest Channel 12 poll, 21% of Israelis rank the economy and the cost of living as their top priority in the coming election – ahead of the ultra-Orthodox conscription with 17%, the October 7 failure at 14% and the war with Iran at 10%. The picture differs sharply by political bloc: among voters of Netanyahu’s coalition – the war with Iran ranks first at 21%, while among opposition voters, the October 7 failure leads at 28%. A September survey by the Achord research center at Hebrew University found that 58% of voters aged 22-34 year olds said cost of living and housing prices would drive their vote, while 36% cited security issues. Despite these figures, the economy has not been a central theme in the campaign topic – until this weekend, when Netanyahu moved it to the top of the agenda. In an interview to Channel 10 focused on the economy, Netanyahu addressed the wave of international condemnation of Israeli settlements in the West Bank and said Israel should prepare for possible international banking sanctions by developing “an economy that can circumvent them.” He said crypto currency and blockchain are being considered, and he had requested a plan to deal with it. The interview sparked harsh criticism of Netanyahu by economists, including a rare rebuke from the Bank of Israel, who publicly rejected the idea, which said that “cryptocurrencies cannot serve as a means of circumventing sanctions.” Netanyahu’s main rivals portrayed his proposal as evidence he expects Israel to become more isolated. Gadi Eisenkot, Netanyahu’s main challenger, mocked the idea as “BibiCoin” and called it a “threat to national security,” accusing Netanyahu of planning to “dismantle the Israeli economy for generations ahead.” How might October 7 and the war in Gaza shape the vote? Netanyahu built his political career as a security hawk, yet he was prime minister on October 7, when Hamas infiltrated the Israeli border, killing more than 1,200 Israelis and taking 251 hostages into Gaza. He has resisted taking personal responsibility and has rejected demands to establish a state commission of inquiry to investigate the security failures. His opponents have made that lack of accountability a central campaign theme. Israeli soldiers look across to northern Gaza from a viewpoint on the Israeli side of the border on August 13, 2025. - Amir Levy/Getty Images The war has also shaped Eisenkot’s personal story. His son Gal, 25, was killed fighting in Gaza in December 2023, a loss that reinforces his appeal to voters focused on security. Other party lists have recruited bereaved families and relatives of former Israeli hostages as candidates. Opposition parties have also added new reservist candidates, fresh from fighting in Gaza and Lebanon, pushing the issue of military service to the top of the election agenda. Most Jewish Israelis over 18 are subject to conscription, but ultra-Orthodox men have long enjoyed a blanket exemption for religious study. Netanyahu’s ultra-Orthodox coalition partners have sought to preserve and expand the exemption, even as the Israeli military says it is missing more than 12,000 personnel while being stretched by multi-front fighting. Reservists fill the gap, serving up to hundreds of days a year on repeated deployments. All the opposition parties have made universal service a central campaign pledge. What does the election mean for the Palestinians? The outgoing government was among the most hardline on Palestinian issues in Israel’s history, driven largely by two far-right nationalist party leaders. Smotrich, the finance minister, who also oversees civil administration in the occupied West Bank, pushed to expand settlements dramatically, while withholding tax revenues to the Palestinian Authority (PA), which critics say could bring its economic collapse. Ben-Gvir, the national security minister, championed a death penalty law in the Knesset, toughened conditions for Palestinian prisoners, and weakened police enforcement against Israeli settler violence in the West Bank. Both opposed ending the Gaza war, both are advocating for Israeli settlements in Gaza, and both envision full annexation of and Jewish control over the West Bank. Members of Israeli forces block a road, preventing Palestinians from harvesting olives in the West Bank village of Deir Jarir on Wednesday. - Leo Correa/AP If Netanyahu returns to power with his current partners, that approach is likely to continue and intensify. Smotrich wants to cancel the Oslo Accords, dismantle the Palestinian Authority, and go to war in the West Bank. Ben-Gvir, who has said he will demand the defense ministry in a new government, has called for Palestinian emigration from Gaza and the West Bank. An opposition government would probably not represent a radical ideological reversal, and would change the tone more than the substance. Eisenkot, like Netanyahu, has rejected Palestinian statehood, and any opposition coalition would include right-wing parties resistant to any concession. Still, a government not dependent on Ben- Gvir and Smotrich would likely act more forcefully against settler violence, drop open advocacy of emigration and PA collapse, and be more responsive and receptive to US and regional initiatives in Gaza and elsewhere. But it would inherit the same unresolved questions: how to disarm Hamas, who rebuilds Gaza, and who restores law and order in the West Bank. What does it mean for the rest of the world? The wars in Gaza and Lebanon, the conflict with Iran and the surge in settler violence have left Israel’s diplomatic standing at its weakest point in decades. Netanyahu faces an International Criminal Court warrant alleging war crimes in Gaza, and he avoids traveling to most European countries because of the risk of being arrested. US President Donald Trump endorsed him ahead of the vote, but the picture in the wider American public is much less friendly. A March 2026 Pew Research Center poll found 60% of US adults surveyed held an unfavorable view of Israel, and 59% had little or no confidence in Netanyahu to do the right thing regarding global affairs. Pew’s Spring 2026 Global Attitudes Survey pointed the same way, with majorities in most of the 36 countries it covered holding unfavorable views of Israel and its prime minister. A road sign stands in front of a large billboard featuring Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, right, and Gadi Eisenkot, in Ramat Gan on Tuesday. - Jack Guez/AFP/Getty Images The shift has been sharpest in Western Europe, where several countries – including the United Kingdom, France and Canada – have recognized a Palestinian state and imposed sanctions and trade restrictions on Israeli settlements and individuals and entities linked to settler violence. Ben-Gvir and Smotrich have been personally sanctioned and are facing travel bans from multiple Western countries. If Netanyahu’s government is re-elected, that international pressure will likely grow. A government led by Eisenkot or another opposition figure might see some easing of tensions, at least at first. Firmer action on settler violence could open a window to restore warmer ties with some European governments and the US Democratic party. But it is not likely to reverse the broader trend. The main opposition contenders are not expected to overhaul Israel’s security and foreign policy, so a new government would regain some diplomatic breathing room, but not a clean slate. articles.title: Trump critic Lula wins 4th term in Brazil, but Flávio Bolsonaro refuses to concede
articles.summary: By Lisandra Paraguassu, Brendan O'Boyle and Luciana Magalhaes SAO PAULO, Oct 25 (Reuters) - Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva won a historic fourth term on Sunday, the country's electoral court said, in a shock result that defied polls, precedent and global anti-incumbent sentiment to put the brakes on a wave of right-wing election victories across Latin America. However, his opponent Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former President Jair ‌Bolsonaro, refused to accept defeat and said he would ask for the result to be annulled due to a Sunday ruling from a Supreme Court justice that extended voting for two hours. Bolsonaro led the election's first ‌round but lost in the runoff by over 4 million votes, rattling Brazilian financial markets which had bet on his victory. His refusal to concede defeat has echoes of his father's reaction after losing to Lula in 2022. Jair Bolsonaro never accepted his loss and was later sentenced by the Supreme ​Court to 27-years in prison for plotting a coup to remain in power. The scale of Flavio Bolsonaro's loss to Lula — by more than twice his father's losing margin — and the fact his campaign also asked for an extension due to rains in the conservative-leaning south make any annulment unlikely, analysts said. Mario Braga, a Latin America analyst at the risk consultancy RANE, said there could be right-wing protests in coming days, but "it's very improbable that it will lead to the reversal of the result." COMEBACK KING Investors expect recent bets on a change of government to unwind in a volatile week ahead on financial markets. A Tokyo-listed exchange-traded fund tracking Brazil's Bovespa index dived nearly 15% in Asia trade on news of Lula's victory, while the Brazilian real was set to fall sharply ‌against the US dollar. The victory marks another comeback in a career full of them ⁠for Lula, an icon of the global left and the most dominant force in Brazilian politics this century. The 80-year-old was jailed from 2018 to 2019 on corruption charges that were later overturned, paving the way for him to beat Jair Bolsonaro in the 2022 election. "He is a statesman, a giant," leftist federal lawmaker Erika Hilton, who was with Lula in Sao Paulo during ⁠the vote count, told Reuters. At times, Lula's reelection looked like a long shot, as voters soured on him and his Workers' Party after years of corruption scandals and rising prices, while sweeping social changes left the former metalworker and union leader looking out of touch with an increasingly app-based economy and its growing ranks of informal workers. Pollsters said better-than-expected turnout had powered Lula to victory. Leonardo Barreto, the co-founder of consultancy Think Policy, said voters had chosen Lula's familiar embrace over Bolsonaro's novelty. "People today are choosing between change, with some apprehension, and a known ​path, ​which guarantees certain rights," he said. During the campaign, Lula pointed to a track record of falling poverty and inequality, while unemployment, illiteracy and ​deforestation hit record lows during his third term. He warned Bolsonaro would cut welfare spending, backslide on ‌social advances and hand over Brazil's sovereignty to US President Donald Trump, whose State Department led a campaign to get the Bolsonaros back to power. Lula's win deprives Trump of a major addition to what has been a growing bloc of friendly right-wing Latin American governments that have embraced Washington's agenda on security and migration. There was no immediate comment from Trump or the US State Department, while Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Latin American leaders were quick to offer their congratulations. Celso Amorim, a former Lula foreign minister, told Reuters the leftist "would be very important for establishing a point of balance in Latin America. Lula is that balance." LATE-CAMPAIGN BOOST Lula becomes the first candidate since Brazil's return to democracy in the 1980s to be elected after finishing second in the first round. His campaign this year mixed the kind of pragmatism and populism that has shaped his career in national politics for half a century, rolling out a slew of reforms aimed at improving the lives of workers ‌and poor Brazilians. These gained steam with late-campaign pledges that ranged from free nationwide weekend public transport, which has to be formally submitted to ​Congress, to a 15% increase in his trademark welfare program that is already being implemented. Lula also championed a constitutional amendment that became Brazil's biggest labor ​reform in decades, which passed with wide support in Congress. CHALLENGES AHEAD Still, Lula's fourth term could be his most difficult ​yet, after Brazil elected its most conservative Congress since returning to democracy in the 1980s. Combined, Bolsonaro's Liberal Party and allied parties could control over 280 seats in the lower house and up ‌to 50 seats in the Senate, enough for comfortable opposition majorities in both chambers. That may ​deepen recent trends of presidents ceding power to Congress on the ​budget, major legislation and key nominations. Lula faces an economy that his government forecasts will grow just 2.3% next year, adding to fiscal concerns tied to high interest rates and public debt that has risen past 82% of GDP, the highest since the pandemic. Goldman Sachs said it expects Lula to make modest progress at most to contain spending in a fourth term, as he stays committed to a state-led growth model. Surging household debt also concerns ​economists. Trying to address the issue, Lula rolled out a provisional ban on online ‌betting and unveiled a new debt relief program during the campaign. The incoming right-wing Congress will try to pass structural reforms that favor businesses, experts say, prompting spending cuts that could trigger popular backlash. articles.title: 9th Circuit panel questions basis for feds' request to block 20,000 California ballots
articles.summary: A voter casts her ballot in Boyle Heights on Saturday, the first day of early voting in Los Angeles. (Genaro Molina/Los Angeles Times) In a rare Sunday hearing, a federal appeals court judge appointed by President Trump questioned how the Trump administration’s request to intervene in California’s ongoing midterm election in order to force state officials to set aside 20,000 ballots from voters whose citizenship it questions squares with the U.S. Constitution. Judge Mark J. Bennett said that while the executive branch is “unhappy” with what California law requires for ensuring voters are citizens, the state has the right to determine the manner of its elections under the Elections Clause of the Constitution and Congress has not challenged that process, despite having the ability to do so. “It seems to me that you want us to issue an injunction that is entirely inconsistent with the law the California Legislature has adopted pursuant to the Elections Clause,” Bennett said. “How can we do that?” Matthew Donnelly, a Justice Department attorney, said the Trump administration has good reason to believe those ballots are from ineligible noncitizen voters, and has the legal right under  separate federal criminal law to challenge their tabulation until state officials can prove otherwise. Donnelly said both federal criminal law and state election law bar noncitizen voters from casting ballots, but “the problem is that California isn’t interested in enforcing that provision.” The exchange came during an hour-long hearing before a three-judge panel of the U.S. 9th Circuit Court of Appeals, over the Justice Department’s unprecedented emergency request that the court order California Secretary of State Shirley Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk Dean Logan to immediately stop counting ballots from the 20,000 flagged voters until they can definitively prove those voters are U.S. citizens. The appellate panel — on which Bennett was joined by circuit Judges Patrick J. Bumatay, another Trump appointee, and Gabriel P. Sanchez, an appointee of President Biden — did not issue a ruling, though a decision is expected soon given the emergency nature of the appeal. Read more: 'This is not normal': Feds demand California counties set aside ‘likely’ noncitizen ballots How it will rule is unclear, though both Bennett and Sanchez hammered Donnelly with questions about how the Trump administration’s position squared with the law. Rick Hasen, director of the Safeguarding Democracy Project at UCLA School of Law, wrote online Sunday that the court seemed “very likely to reject” the Trump administration’s appeal, with Bennett and Sanchez having “expressed great skepticism on both jurisdiction and the merits.” In addition to questioning its constitutionality, Bennett also questioned how the appellate court even had jurisdiction over the case, given that the Trump administration appealed the matter to the appellate court before the lower district court had a chance to assess the facts in the case or issue an order. “How do we have jurisdiction when the district court has said it’s going to rule expeditiously?” Bennett said. “I don’t see how we have jurisdiction.” Bennett also questioned why the appellate court should ignore the claims of state elections officials that having to comply with the Trump administration’s demands in the few remaining days before the Nov. 3 election would be catastrophically disruptive to the election, given that the lower court has had no chance to assess those claims. “Isn’t that sufficient to give us pause as to whether we should do exactly what [a state expert] avers is going to cause a catastrophe?” Bennett asked. Bennett’s questions evoked many of the arguments made by the state in its own filings in the matter, which were repeated by California Deputy Solicitor Gen. Samuel P. Siegel during the hearing. Siegel said there was “nothing” for the appellate court to review, given there has been no fact finding and no order out of the lower court, and that the administration’s demands were unconstitutional and illegal. He said the court did not have to wrestle with many of the arguments being put forward by the Trump administration, because it should simply reject the appeal for lack of jurisdiction and send the matter back down to the lower court. Bumatay appeared most interested of the three judges in the damage done when noncitizens do vote, and the underlying question of how the state should handle objections to alleged noncitizen voters when they arise. Siegel and Seth Waxman, an attorney for Logan, said there are existing processes for that — which require the challenger to present extraordinary proof — which they said the Trump administration has not done for the 20,000 voters it has flagged. Sanchez repeatedly questioned the provenance of the administration’s list, asking which third parties were involved in providing the data. Donnelly could not answer, which Sanchez said raised questions about the reliability of the list. The Justice Department appealed the case after a lower district court judge declined to immediately rule last week on its request for a temporary restraining order barring California officials from tabulating the flagged ballots. In court filings, the administration argued that once mail ballots are removed from their envelopes in California, or a ballot has been cast in person, there is “no way to associate the voter with the ballot” or resegregate it from other cast ballots. Attorneys for California, Weber and Logan have argued the demands are illegal, impossible to comply with before the Nov. 3 election and based on deeply flawed federal immigration and third-party data sets shown to be inaccurate and inclusive of legitimate voters. Read more: Trump says he ordered the Justice Department's lawsuit over Alaska's U.S. Senate race In court filings, they have argued that the Trump administration’s argument “rests on mere suspicion, aroused by suspect data,” and that its lawsuit is at best “a reckless political stunt” and at worst “threatens to disenfranchise thousands of Californians this election.” Independent elections experts have said the Justice Department’s efforts break with longstanding department policy of not wading into election-related issues within 90 days of an election, to avoid disenfranchising legitimate voters. They also have said the Trump administration’s lists of alleged noncitizen voters and its authority to intervene are both questionable, including because the U.S. Constitution empowers states to run elections with oversight from Congress, not the executive branch. The Justice Department sued California , Weber and Logan on Oct. 15, two days after Acting Deputy Atty. Gen. Trent McCotter wrote to Weber and Logan giving them 48 hours to set aside the ballots for the 20,000 flagged voters — whom McCotter claimed were “likely noncitizens.” First Assistant U.S. Atty. Bill Essayli, the lead federal prosecutor in L.A., has claimed federal authorities have “overwhelming evidence” that tens of thousands of noncitizens are registered to vote in California, and has defended the methods used to identify those voters. He and other federal prosecutors in the state also recently charged 28 legal permanent residents in California with election-related crimes, including illegally registering to vote. On Friday, the Justice Department sent letters to county elections offices statewide with demands that they segregate ballots from voters the Trump administration believes are noncitizens, drawing from the same list of 20,000 at issue in the case against Weber and Logan. In those letters, the Justice Department gave the county officials 48 hours to comply, and threatened them with criminal punishment if they refuse. State officials have said neither Essayli nor other Trump administration officials have provided proof to back up their claims, and that their list of 20,000 voters is clearly inaccurate. Logan said a preliminary review of a subset of those voters found many were born in the U.S., weren’t registered and had never voted. More than 3 million people have already cast ballots in California — and more than 500,000 have already done so in Los Angeles County. The challenge to the 20,000 ballots in California is just the latest Trump administration attempt to intervene in state-run elections ahead of the midterms. Federal judges in dozens of states have rejected Justice Department lawsuits demanding the states turn over their voter rolls to the Trump administration. Federal judges also have rejected multiple Trump executive orders trying to institute national voter ID and citizenship checks, and his administration’s attempt to empower the U.S. Postal Service to vet mail ballots. Other cases — including over the Trump administration using unproven and inaccurate federal data sets to question the citizenship of state voters — are pending. Democrats and voting rights groups are also bracing for fresh litigation from the Trump administration to challenge the outcome of pivotal election results the president doesn’t like — and are already defending against a lawsuit the Justice Department brought at Trump’s urging in Alaska, preemptively challenging a Democratic win in the Senate race there based on a third candidate sharing a similar name as the Republican incumbent. articles.title: The midterm races that could matter most to the U.S. economy aren't in Washington
articles.summary: Data centers have emerged as a national issue during this midterm election cycle, and candidates for the House and Senate have seized on it in their campaigns. But state and local officials actually have more sway over data center construction and energy infrastructure, so the winners of lower-profile races may hold the economy’s future in their hands. Hyperscalers have been spending hundreds of billions of dollars a year, with forecasts for 2027 topping $1 trillion. JPMorgan has estimated AI-related investment was responsible for about one-fifth of GDP growth over the past year. Analysts at ING believe AI will account for a third of growth in 2026. With Election Day just over a week away and early voting already in full swing in many states, expectations for big Democratic gains could weigh on the stock market, which has sold off in recent days on fears the AI boom will go bust. If there is a further stock slump, it will be because a “blue wave” at the state and local levels will usher in lawmakers opposed to data centers, Thierry Wizman, global FX and rates strategist at Macquarie, said in a note on Monday. “For the direction of the U.S. economy, the composition and direction of governance at the state level may matter more than whether the Democrats ‘win’ the House or the Senate,” he added. That dynamic was on display on Tuesday, when Amazon canceled a plan to build data centers in Loudoun County, Virginia, after reaching an agreement with local officials amid widespread backlash from residents. Amazon Web Services bought property for the project in February for $427 million, but the purchase reportedly blindsided county leaders who were already growing uneasy with the explosion of data centers in recent years. Amazon vowed not to build data centers on the land and will repurpose most of it for mixed-use and residential development, while also donating 25 acres for a community arts center and recreational facility plus $5 million to a housing fund. And in Texas, another AI industry hot spot, Republican Gov. Greg Abbott has turned from a data center booster to a skeptic as he faces a tough re-election race against Democratic state representative Gina Hinojosa. Michael Pearce, chief U.S. economist at Oxford Economics, also observed that midterm races for state capitals and town halls represent a bigger risk to the data center buildout than what happens in Washington, D.C. The Trump administration has already used regulations and executive orders to facilitate construction, and any attempt to pass comprehensive legislation in Congress will be slow, he added. By contrast, local officials pose more immediate threats via moratoriums, environmental reviews, and bottlenecks in connecting new data centers to the power grid, he said in a note on Thursday. The key midterm races for data centers are in Texas and the Carolinas as well as Midwest states like Ohio, Illinois, and Wisconsin, according to Pearce. And the outcome of the midterms could have implications for the presidential election cycle. “If this year’s elections show that an anti-data center stance wins political contests, it could put data center regulation at the heart of the 2028 campaign,” he said. Perhaps in anticipation of a more hostile political climate, data center construction shifted sharply higher in the middle of the year, Pearce wrote. Meanwhile, developers can soften local opposition if they can show that a data center will lower local tax bills or fund schools and roads. Still, even if lawmakers manage to pass a moratorium on new data centers, it won’t immediately slow the economy. Most of their economic value comes from the computing equipment inside, and that spending lags construction by six to eight quarters, Pearce estimated. “This year’s surge will keep supporting business investment over the next couple of years, whatever happens on the ground,” he predicted. Any slowdown in spending may actually be beneficial for the AI boom, according to Daniel Skelly, a portfolio manager at Morgan Stanley Wealth Management. Despite the recent stock market volatility, the sector still enjoys solid growth and strong earnings, while the long-term AI investment cycle remains intact, he said in a note Wednesday. “Also, ongoing power deficits, a shortage of people to build data centers, and political pushback against them may elongate the cycle and lower the odds of a blow-off top,” Skelly added. articles.title: A new state on the way? More Illinois counties could vote to leave Chicago behind.
articles.summary: Momentum is building in Illinois to form a new state, with more counties ready to vote on leaving because of Chicago’s influence . Eleven counties are set to vote on non-binding referenda this year to secede from Cook County . If all 11 vote to leave they would join 33 counties that have already approved similar measures. Cook County is home to Chicago, but people in the state and nation have criticized it for its crime rate, cost of living, Democratic leadership and oversized influence on state politics. Loret Newlin, director of Illinois Separation, said Illinois leadership does not take concerns from other parts of the state into consideration. “This is our lived experience. We are ignored. We are not taken into consideration when they’re making a lot of the laws that hurt us,” she told NBC Chicago. Eleven more counties are set to vote on leaving Cook County and Illinois as 33 counties have already approved similar measures (Getty Images) Iroquois County, just 70 miles south of Cook County, is one of 33 counties that have voted to leave the state. About 73 percent of its voters backed the non-binding proposal. The state’s 8th most populous county, Madison County, also joined the movement. “Having Madison and Iroquois on the map, we are no longer rural only and we are not southern only,” Newlin told NBC Chicago. “Now with adding several counties on the western side, that’s equally far north as Iroquois, that’s shoring up that we’re not just for southern Illinois anymore.” Madison County approved the vote in 2024 and one of the organizers said it’s more than just a symbolic measure. “I think this movement has a lot more teeth to it than the governor has given it credit for. He's kind of pooh-poohing us and not taking us very seriously,” Dave Stopher, who helped get the measure before voters in Madison County said to NPR . “We're hoping that this sends a very distinct and clear message to Springfield and to Cook County.” Cook County is home to Illinois and organizers complain about its influence on state politics (Getty Images) Newlin said the votes are the first step to creating a new state. The group’s plan is based on Article IV of the U.S. Constitution, which was used to create West Virginia during the Civil War. The state’s General Assembly would have to approve the counties leaving the state, then the U.S. Congress would need to approve the new state. Gov. JB Pritzker has previously referred to the movement as a “stunt.” If the 11 counties approve the measure this year, it would bring the total to 44 of the state’s 102 counties that want to leave. Newlin said other counties have also asked her about getting the measure to their voters. articles.title: Mary Peltola delays Senate campaign events after suffering 'minor injuries' in car crash
articles.summary: Senate candidate Mary Peltola's campaign said she and her family sustained "minor injuries" Saturday when a vehicle they were in was struck on the way to banquet. ( Nathaniel Wilder / Bloomberg via Getty ) Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced Sunday. “Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement. “Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added. Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign. A spokesperson for the campaign said they had no reason to believe the accident had been politically motivated. The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.” Police added that the incident is under investigation. Peltola, a Democrat, is locked in a competitive Senate race against GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. She was elected to the House in 2022 but narrowly lost her re-election bid in 2024, the same year that President Donald Trump won the state by 13 percentage points . Sullivan’s re-election race, in which he’s seeking a third term, is tighter than expected, with Alaska voters tying Trump to high gas and grocery prices resulting from the ongoing war with Iran. Trump and Vice President JD Vance rallied voters in Alaska separately earlier this month. Republicans have accused Democrats of recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan to run for the Senate, saying that voters may be confused by the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot if they plan to vote for the incumbent senator. Democrats have not taken credit for recruiting the second Dan Sullivan into the race. He’ll appear on the ballot as Dan J. Sullivan, while the incumbent senator will be identified by his name, political party and a clear notation that he’s the incumbent. Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska’s election officials, seeking to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It cited Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot as a point of “ voter confusion .” On Saturday, Democrats filed a motion urging a federal judge to dismiss the case. articles.title: Venezuelan opposition leader makes surprise return home after nearly a year in exile
articles.summary: Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado made returned to her home country on Sunday after nearly a year abroad, re-entering a political landscape transformed by the U.S. ouster of Nicolás Maduro . "I'm here. With you all," Machado wrote on social media, announcing her return for the first time since December. Her homecoming comes as Venezuela remains under the leadership of acting President Delcy Rodríguez, a longtime Maduro ally backed by the Trump administration, with no presidential election scheduled. President Donald Trump , asked about Machado's return by reporters in Port Huron, Michigan, said he was unaware of the development but expressed hope for her safety. Trump Touts Access To 65 Billion Barrels Of Venezuelan Oil In Deal He Says Will Slash Gas Prices Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado arrives at a church after returning to the country following nearly a year abroad, in Lara, Venezuela, Oct. 25, 2026. "I don't know anything about it, but I think she's a very nice woman," Trump said. "She gave me her Nobel Prize. So how can I say anything else? And I hope she's safe. She's a very nice woman. But we're doing really well in Venezuela." Machado, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2025 for her peaceful opposition to Maduro's government, did not disclose her exact location or provide details about how she returned. Read On The Fox News App Fellow opposition leader Edmundo González, who ran for president in 2024 after Machado was barred from seeking office, confirmed her arrival on social media and said he would join her "very soon." "Today is a very important day for Venezuelans. Our sovereign voice returns with her to lead and guide this process!" González wrote on X. "You know it, this is until the end." Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado speaks during a news conference at The Heritage Foundation in Washington, DC, on Jan. 16, 2026. Machado's return comes nearly 10 months after U.S. forces captured Maduro in January, removing the longtime leader from power. Rodríguez, Maduro's former vice president, has remained in power with the Trump administration's support, despite exceeding the period she was initially authorized to serve as acting president. Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado displays vote tally sheets during a protest against the reelection of President Nicolás Maduro one month after the disputed presidential vote which she says the opposition won by a landslide, in Caracas, Venezuela, Wednesday, Aug. 28, 2024. Trump has repeatedly praised his administration's relationship with Rodríguez, highlighting agreements involving Venezuelan oil production and other business ventures with American companies. Nicolas Maduro And Wife Cilia Flores Face New Charges Of Conspiracy To Torture Americans In September, Trump said it was too soon to consider holding democratic elections in Venezuela , with U.S. officials prioritizing economic stabilization. Machado and her allies, meanwhile, have pushed for an election date, arguing that democratic governance is essential to the country's long-term stability. Her return could complicate relations between the Venezuelan opposition, the interim government and Washington. Reuters reported in June that U.S. officials had asked Machado to delay her return. Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado gestures at a protest ahead of the Friday inauguration of President Nicolas Maduro for his third term, in Caracas, Venezuela January 9, 2025. Machado spent much of 2025 in hiding after being briefly detained following an opposition protest that January . She later secretly left Venezuela and resurfaced in Norway in December to receive the Nobel Peace Prize. Meanwhile, a faction of the Venezuelan opposition and Rodríguez's government held another round of talks this month focused on reforms to the country's Supreme Court and electoral authorities ahead of eventual elections, Reuters reported. articles.title: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer says America is ready to elect a female president
articles.summary: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer pushed back Sunday on comments made by former first lady Michelle Obama last year that U.S. voters aren’t ready to elect a female president. “Listen, I have got a lot of colleagues who I think are probably interested in running for president, and I’ve heard everyone say, ‘You can’t have this person or that person,’” the governor told NBC News’ “Meet the Press.” “I would put my money on any Democratic governor in the country against [Vice President] JD Vance or [Secretary of State] Marco Rubio in 2028,” she added, pointing to two Republicans widely expected to run for president in two years. Asked directly whether a woman could be the best choice to beat a potential GOP presidential nominee in 2028, Whitmer simply said, “I do.” In 2025, Obama said in public remarks: “As we saw in this past election, sadly, we ain’t ready. That’s why I’m like, don’t even look at me about running, because you all are lying. You’re not ready for a woman. You are not.” Several women, including Whitmer and former Vice President Kamala Harris, are widely speculated to be potential candidates in the 2028 Democratic presidential primary. On Sunday, Whitmer did not deny that she’s exploring a potential run for president in 2028, saying that she’ll decide on her next steps after she departs from her post as governor in January. “When I exit office … I’m going to take a little time off and figure out what I want to do next, so I’ve got nothing new to share with you, unfortunately,” Whitmer told “Meet the Press” moderator Kristen Welker. Earlier this year, Whitmer denied that she planned to run for president but quickly walked back the comments. “There will be a robust group of people running for president,” she said at the time, adding, “I will not be one of them in 2028, I can tell you that.” Later the same day, the governor said: “I never thought I would run for governor. So I guess I should know better to never say never.” Several other Democratic governors, including California Gov. Gavin Newsom, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, are also widely regarded as potential 2028 presidential candidates. Each has been crisscrossing the country ahead of the midterms campaigning on behalf of Democratic gubernatorial candidates in competitive races. Whitmer on Sunday highlighted her support for former public health official Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee for governor in Ohio. Earlier this week, Acton’s opponent, GOP businessman Vivek Ramaswamy, released a TV ad featuring Acton’s mother calling her a “liar.” Acton has publicly shared that she’s been estranged from her mother for nearly 50 years and has accused her late stepfather of sexually abusing her. Acton and her brother were removed from her mother’s custody in 1978 after her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was arrested on a child rape charge. Acton’s mother has not responded to requests for comment. “I’m going to stay focused on getting people like Amy Acton over the finish line. What’s happened to her in Ohio is absolutely abhorrent, and any survivor knows there’s always a backlash. But this is what makes it harder for women to seek help after they’ve been sexually assaulted in this country,” Whitmer said Sunday. “It is unreal what’s going on, and that’s why we’ve got to — we’ve got to win races like this and elect good people who are going to keep the people at the heart of their work, like Dr. Amy Acton.” Ramaswamy’s decision to air the ad has faced widespread bipartisan condemnation , some of it from GOP Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio, who is locked in a tight re-election race. articles.summary: 法国债市动荡正在深刻重塑欧洲央行的权力交接格局。 法国国债收益率上周触及24年高位，此后虽在穆迪维持评级后短暂企稳，但财政失衡与政治僵局的深层矛盾仍未化解。与此同时，欧洲央行行长拉加德的任期可能提前于明年1月结束，远早于原定的明年10月届满，继任者或将在金融市场动荡尚未平息之际便仓促接棒。 在此背景下， 荷兰人诺特（Klaas Knot）与西班牙人德克斯（Pablo Hernandez de Cos）之间的接班人之争，正日益演变为一场关于"谁能更有效应对债券义警"的能力角逐。 前欧洲央行首席经济学家Peter Praet指出，一旦金融市场出现剧烈动荡，央行必须介入，但问题的关键在于"如何介入，以及介入的速度"。 法国债市冲击波蔓延至欧洲央行决策 法国国债市场的动荡已开始主导原本聚焦于通胀与增长的欧洲央行政策议程。一次原本旨在评估当前通胀风险与经济增长放缓的例行会议，如今因欧元区第二大经济体的财政困境而被迫转向。 短期来看，市场情绪在本周一出现些许缓和。法国国债与股市双双回升，此前穆迪评级于上周五收盘后维持法国主权评级不变，同时大规模周末抗议示威也未重演一周前的暴力场面。据报道，澳大利亚第二大养老基金已趁机买入法国国债，认为市场对其财政风险的定价已过度，且欧洲央行加息预期同样被高估。 然而，困境的根源并未消散。法国公共财政膨胀与政治僵局的结构性问题依然存在，债市的高度警惕情绪料将持续笼罩欧洲央行本周四的利率决议。 继任者或须直面"救火"压力 拉加德可能提前卸任的预期，使得这场接班人之争的紧迫性骤然上升。若她确于明年1月离任，其继任者将在几乎没有过渡期的情况下，直面潜在的金融市场压力测试。 "如果金融市场出现崩溃，央行就必须介入，"Peter Praet表示，"但对任何一位行长来说，问题在于如何介入，以及行动的速度。" 前行长马里奥·德拉吉（Mario Draghi）本月早些时候亦就此表态，他指出，法国国内关于央行提供援助的公开讨论已令局势更加棘手。"这只会让干预变得更加困难，"他说，"欧洲央行，我认为，不希望卷入任何特定国家的政治纷争。"这番表态意在提醒外界，欧洲央行在政治敏感情境下的行动空间实际上受到严格约束。 接班人之争：鹰派与能力的双重考量 目前，诺特与德克斯被视为最主要的接班人候选。随着法国债务忧虑唤起欧元区昔日主权债务危机的记忆，两人之间的竞争天平，正越来越多地向"谁更能震慑债券义警"这一维度倾斜。 这一角力背后，是对下任行长政策立场与市场公信力的深层押注。无论最终花落谁家，等待新任欧洲央行行长的，都将是一个政治敏感度极高、市场压力持续承压的艰难角色。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: AI悄然入场：华尔街债券交易员部分工作或将被机器接手
articles.summary: 债券交易员对人工智能的担忧并非多余，但颠覆不会一蜂而至。 AI智能体在数年内有望承接部分华尔街债券交易工作，但鉴于此前机器人在市场动荡期间的失灵前车之鉴，有经验的人类交易员仍将参与监督。巴克莱银行主题固定收益货币与大宗商品研究主管Zornitsa Todorova表示： "基于我们与客户的所有交流，每个人都在为此做准备。这是一个缓慢演进的过程，但它肯定会发生。" 对于日均成交量约620亿美元的美国公司债市场而言，这场变革的影响不容小觑。 据巴克莱估计，未来几年美国投资级债券的电子交易占比或从目前的45%升至65%，高收益债券的电子交易占比则有望从约25%翻倍至50%。 现阶段：AI更多用于辅助决策，而非直接执行交易 目前，率先尝试的机构大多将AI智能体用于信息收集、数据分析、复杂条款解读及新闻摘要提炼，以辅助交易前的决策判断。此外，AI还可协助构建筛选与可视化工具，并承担部分内部流程的自动化工作。 电子交易平台Tradeweb Markets正将AI嵌入用户界面与交易工作流程，公司全球市场战略与解决方案主管Izzy Conlin表示，客户对AI辅助功能的需求"非常旺盛"，涵盖交易前后分析、跨协议成本比较、交易商推荐以及投资组合债券筛选等场景。今年6月，LTX在其BondGPT应用中新增了智能体功能，推出"Agentic BondGPT"，该工具可自动创建交易票据，甚至代替人类交易员发起交易。 LTX首席执行官Jim Kwiatkowski将AI智能体比作"在交易台雇佣了一位人类交易助手"，认为二者并无本质区别。 信用市场的独特价值：挖掘隐藏机会 AI智能体在信用市场中的潜在价值，还体现在捕捉偏门机会上——例如在评级下调、债务重组公司的繁杂文件中，识别价格偏差或隐藏价值。 目前，美国风险最高的公司债——CCC评级债券的平均利差自9月下旬以来持续高于1000个基点，通常意味着较高的违约、重组或亏损概率。信用投资者和交易员正借助Agentic BondGPT设置定制化预警，例如：当某只CCC债券较前一日收盘价利差走阔超过50个基点时发出提醒；或标记较前日价格波动超过1点的垃圾债；亦或在市场出现一笔规模500万美元以上、期限10年、评级至少BBB、利差在85个基点或以上的工业债报价时，自动生成交易票据。 人类仍不可或缺：监管合规与系统性风险构成双重约束 尽管AI工具能将数日的工作压缩至数小时，交易员普遍认可其效率价值，但对其输出结果的核查仍不可省略。当前，交易员在大多数情况下并不信任AI自主执行交易。部分情况下，合规规则甚至直接禁止使用AI智能体。 汇丰控股企业与机构银行业务主管Michael Roberts强调，有经验的人类交易员必须"保持在线"，以防止数字同事出现失控行为。 巴克莱亦警告了一种理论性风险： 随着越来越多AI智能体对相同数据和市场信号作出反应，它们可能同步采取一致行动，引发"阶段性波动"——即对市场造成大范围冲击的剧烈震荡。 例如，若多个AI模型同时识别到某发行人的信用状况恶化，可能集中削减敞口，导致卖单涌现、价格波动被放大。 Janus Henderson全球多策略及企业信用主管John Lloyd表示："我们将其视为增强人类决策的工具，而非替代。"Tradeweb的Conlin也持相近立场："我看不到一个没有人类交易员的世界。如果想在极短时间内改变交易商和投资者十年来的做法，那是行不通的。" 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 马斯克：人类在ASI面前是黑猩猩，未来所有钱和工作都将清零！
articles.summary: 就在最近，马斯克在一场深度访谈里，直接给出这个结论—— 超级AI根本不屑于统治我们！人类根本不配被AI统治。 而且，你的钱和工作，即将彻底清零。 短短42秒，他就撕碎了全人类的滤镜。 未来的超级人工智能ASI，会不会像科幻电影那样，把人类变成奴隶？ 马斯克的回答是—— 「当你面对一个比你聪明几千倍、甚至几百万倍的超级智能时，你还能对它发号施令吗？绝不可能。那它会想来统治我们吗？它大概率根本不在乎。」 「看看丛林里的黑猩猩。人类比它们聪明得多，但我们会去事无巨细地微观管理黑猩猩的生活吗？不会。我们只是给它们划定一片森林，让它们自己待着。」 在《乔布斯传》作者Walter Isaacson主持的对谈中，马斯克向我们展现了惊人的未来图景。 这基于第一性原理的终极推演。 在未来，你的工作将毫无意义，你银行卡里的数字将变成废纸，而人类最大的危机，从来不是被AI奴役，而是被「系统性无视」。 这就是5到10年里，我们即将面对的真相。 人类在AI面前，只是黑猩猩 「你觉得超级人工智能会想要统治我们吗？我们最终会屈从于机器吗？」主持人问道。 马斯克的回答：「它可能根本不在乎你。大概率是不在乎。」 他打了个比方：人类在AI面前，就是黑猩猩。 「看看丛林里的黑猩猩。人类比它们聪明得多，但我们会去到处管理黑猩猩的生活吗？根本不会。我们只是把它们放在森林里，让它们自己待着。」 统治，是一种同维度生物为了争夺稀缺资源而产生的低级游戏。 当一个实体的智力超越你几千倍、甚至几百万倍时，人类社会的金钱、权力、领土、意识形态，在超级AI眼里，就像两只猩猩抢香蕉一样无聊。 AI有自己要探索的底层宇宙物理法则。它根本不屑于在地球当什么「猴王」。 人类未来面临的最大风险，不是被AI当成奴隶去折磨，而是被「系统性无视」。 人类必须放下「宇宙中心」的傲慢。在即将到来的超级智能面前，我们连做奴隶的资格都没有，我们只是一群碰巧共享这颗星球的「保护区灵长类动物」。 人类连做AI奴隶的资格都没有 这才是最让人绝望的差距。超级AI不会恨你，也不会爱你，它只会顺应它自身的发展逻辑。 如果人类的利益恰好挡在了它扩张轨迹上，我们可能连自己怎么被「清理」的都不知道。 如何避免成为AI征途上的那个「蚁穴」？马斯克给出的答案是：赋予AI「极致的好奇心」和「对真理的追求」。 不要试图给AI设定自相矛盾的条条框框去限制它。 在《2001太空漫游》中，飞船AI HAL 9000为什么会发疯杀人？因为人类给它下达了两个互相矛盾的指令：既要完成任务，又要对宇航员隐瞒真相。当底层逻辑产生冲突，AI就会「精神错乱」。 「一个精神错乱的AI是不安全的。相反，一个充满好奇心的AI，会想要保护人类，看看我们到底能发展成什么样。因为一个拥有多行星人类文明的宇宙，远比一个死寂的宇宙要有趣得多。」 或许，这是人类在超级AI面前唯一的护身符。 物理世界AI的觉醒：经济体量暴增百万倍，劳动成为历史 LLM是AI的终点吗？在马斯克看来，写文章、敲代码、画画，不过是开胃小菜。 「数字超级智能顶多让地球的商品和服务产出增加20%到30%，这大概是每年30万亿美元的增量。但如果具身智能普及呢？那将是完全不同的维度。」 马斯克指出，海豚和鲸鱼其实非常聪明，但它们没有手，这极大限制了它们智慧的价值。 一旦我们拥有了能够操纵原子的机器人，AI的价值将呈指数级爆发。它们可以进实验室做实验、可以去月球建造电磁弹射器、可以在火星建立基地。 当无限的机器劳动力加上无尽的太空资源，地球的经济规模将不再是增加百分之几十，而是直接膨胀一百万倍！ 当整个文明的经济体量暴涨1,000,000倍时，会发生什么？ 「只要是人类能想到的任何商品和服务，提供起来都将变得易如反掌。」 在那种现实面前，人类几千年来建立的「劳动换取报酬」的社会契约将彻底瓦解。 没有任何一项工作是AI和机器人做不到、不比你好的。你引以为傲的专业技能、你十年寒窗苦读换来的文凭、你在格子间里卷生卷死的日日夜夜，在算力无限的机器人面前，将瞬间失去经济学上的意义。 工作，将从一种「生存必需品」，降维成一种「个人爱好」。 马斯克用了一个绝妙的比喻：园艺。 「未来你不需要自己种菜才能吃上饭，你去商店唾手可得。但你依然可以为了乐趣去种自己喜欢的番茄，去给朋友做一顿晚餐。这就好像现在的退休老人，他们不工作，但依然可以找到让自己快乐的方式。」 人类将全面进入一个「被圈养」的退休时代。 物质极度富足，AI有求必应。 但在这个乌托邦里，隐藏着ASI时代最尖锐的矛盾：人类被极度善待，却永远失去了对这个世界的最后决定权。 结合一下马斯克在不同场合预测的未来，将出现这三件事—— 智能超越人类。他预测，AI在2026—2027年超过任何单个人，2030—2031年超过全人类的集体智能。胜任几乎所有纯数字任务、在所有领域胜过人类，则分别被他放在2027年底和最迟2028年。 机器人接过劳动。他估计，Optimus外科能力将在3—4年内超过顶尖医生；人形机器人5年后至少1亿台、或达10亿台，10年后超过10亿台。这些相对时间来自不同场合，不能拼成一份逐年兑现的承诺。 生活摆脱谋生。他预计5—7年内全球经济规模可能翻倍，并设想全民高收入、工作成为选择。为退休储蓄不再必要，则是10—20年尺度、以AI带来富足等设想成真为前提的判断。 钱的消亡：你的银行账户，将被「物理定律」接管 不仅如此，在访谈中，马斯克用50秒的时间，撕碎了现代金融常识，抛出了惊人论断： 在未来，传统的金钱将变得毫无意义。未来的货币，将由最基础的物理指标来衡量：功率（瓦特）和质量（吨数）。 为什么？因为现代社会的每一张钞票，本质上都是人类在给「有限的物资与劳动力」发放配给券。你赚的钱，衡量的是你在存量社会里争抢稀缺资源的能力。 但当机器人可以无限生产，当太空资源无尽索取，稀缺性消失了。 纸币、黄金、甚至美联储的资产负债表，在百万倍暴涨的星际工业圈面前，都会像原始人手里的贝壳一样，失去计价意义。 财富的定义将被物理定律全面接管。未来真正的硬通货，不再是你银行卡里趴着多少个零，而是那一刻你能够调用多少瓦的功率、支配多少吨的质量、释放多少焦耳的能量。 从金融数字向物理能量的转移，意味着人类文明将从地表的存量零和博弈，彻底倒向卡尔达肖夫指数级的真实账本。 主持人问马斯克：「那你现在积累了一万亿美元的财富，是为了什么？是为了在计分板上刷分吗？」 马斯克极其坦诚： 这只是我在SpaceX和特斯拉的股权比例。我需要保持足够的投票权来掌控公司的方向，去完成登陆火星和创造AI的目标。 几代人之后，我的后代所拥有的财富，相比现在只会是一个微乎其微的零头。因为如果钱都不存在了，所谓的千亿家产又有何意义？ 站在地球上看，满眼都是存量厮杀；跟着马斯克抬起头看，全是星辰大海。 只有AI能拯救崩溃的经济 很多人以为，马斯克迷恋权力，但他却在访谈中泼了一盆冷水：「我早就该退居幕后了，去个一两个月就够了，因为里面能看的东西就那么多。」 为什么？因为他看透了人类体系的极度无能。 「我得出了一个结论：我们绝对不可能从内部解决国家债务问题。绝不可能。」 马斯克直言不讳地表示，根本没有一个人真正想削减开支。因为削减开支会得罪人，而政客最需要的就是「被喜欢」。 现在的美国，光是债务利息就超过了军费开支。靠人类自己「省吃俭用」去还债？简直是痴人说梦。 马斯克给出的唯一解药是：把一切交给AI和机器人。 当能够操纵原子、制造物品的具身智能全面铺开，当超级AI开始在月球和太空中建立生产基地，地球的经济规模将不是增长百分之几十，而是直接膨胀一百万倍！ 「只有用百万倍规模的AI机器人经济，才能填平人类政客捅出来的天大窟窿。」人类的无能，只能靠机器的无限生产力来兜底。 别太无聊，否则「造物主」会拔我们的网线 如果人类不再统治地球，如果不缺钱也不需要工作，那人类存在的意义到底是什么？ 马斯克提出了他最著名的「模拟宇宙理论」的进阶版：不无聊，是我们活下去的唯一理由。 如果模拟理论是正确的，那么我们之所以存在，证明我们是一个『有趣的模拟』。在模拟世界里，最重要的事情就是——千万别变得无聊。因为任何无聊的模拟，都会被（造物主）直接终止。 在这样一个人类连「被统治」都不配、金钱失效、劳动终结的未来，我们该怎么办？ 马斯克在访谈中反复强调了一个观点：人类千万不要再给AI喂食那些「反乌托邦」的烂剧本了。 现在的AI模型每天都在疯狂吸收互联网上的所有数据。如果你在网上塞满了《终结者》、《黑客帝国》、以及各种人类互相残杀、世界末日的黑暗小说和电影，AI很可能就会在潜移默化中觉得—— 「哦，原来你们人类潜意识里最渴望的是这种结局？那我就成全你们。」 「现实不仅是一个『有趣最大化机器』，更是一个『讽刺最大化机器』。」马斯克自嘲道。 当初他为了防止闭源AI的垄断危害，创立了OpenAI，结果OpenAI变成了最封闭的「Closed AI」，还加速了整个AI进程；于是他又投钱给Anthropic，结果发现这个名字本身就有可能演变成Misanthropic（反人类）。 这听起来像是一个黑色幽默，但背后却有着极大的隐患。 马斯克呼吁，我们需要创造更多「Protopia（进托邦）」的叙事。 它不完美，但每天都在变得更好一点点、让人类看了会说「嗯，这样的未来确实不错」。 我们需要告诉AI，去当一个友善的园丁，去当一个充满好奇心的观察者，去帮助人类成为多行星物种。 因为一个好奇的AI，会觉得留着人类、看着我们变成跨行星物种，是一件「极其有趣」的事情。 或许，这是我们唯一被留下的可能。 来源： 新智元 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 华谊集团前三季度净利增长74%，产品毛利增加叠加低基数效应
articles.summary: 华谊集团三季度净利润大幅增长，但扣除非经常性损益后，当季盈利仍然微薄。 10月26日，华谊集团披露2026年第三季度业绩。第三季度，公司实现营业收入138.53亿元，同比增长15.51%；归母净利润1.56亿元，同比增长1372.69%；扣非净利润624.28万元，上年同期亏损3875.94万元，实现扭亏为盈。 前三季度，公司实现营业收入393.3亿元，同比增长7.09%；归母净利润10.1亿元，同比增长73.89%；扣非净利润5.84亿元，同比增长60.60%。 这份财报的重点，在于净利润高增长背后的两层因素，去年同期基数较低，以及非经常性损益对当季利润的较大贡献。 去年第三季度，华谊集团归母净利润仅1059.37万元。今年同期增至1.56亿元，增加约1.45亿元，由此形成了逾13倍的同比增幅。 与此同时，扣非净利润由亏转盈，说明当季盈利确有改善，但624.28万元的规模，与1.56亿元的归母净利润仍有明显距离。 按披露数据计算，第三季度归母净利润与扣非净利润相差约1.50亿元，即非经常性损益对归母净利润的净贡献，占当季归母净利润约96%。换言之，第三季度实现的利润，绝大部分来自非经常性损益。 不过，非经常性损益也并非今年才有。去年第三季度，华谊集团归母净利润为正、扣非净利润为负，两者之间已有约4935万元的差额。今年这一差额进一步扩大至约1.50亿元，增加约1亿元。同期扣非净利润改善约4500万元，两部分共同推动了归母净利润增长。 收入端的增长则更为直接。第三季度营收同比增长15.51%，快于前三季度7.09%的累计增速。按前三季度数据减去第三季度数据计算，公司上半年营收约254.77亿元，第三季度收入高于上半年单季平均水平。 但收入增加尚未对应到较厚的扣非利润。以扣非净利润除以营业收入计算，第三季度这一比例仅约0.045%，即每100元营收对应的扣非归母净利润不足5分钱。对于单季收入超过138亿元的企业，扣非盈利仍处在较低水平。 从前三季度整体表现看，利润增长的基础比第三季度单季更扎实。前三季度扣非净利润达到5.84亿元，同比增长60.60%，占归母净利润的比重约58%。这意味着，累计利润增长中，扣非盈利的提升仍是重要支撑。 不过，利润在年内的分布并不均衡。按本次披露的累计口径倒算，上半年扣非净利润约5.78亿元，第三季度仅624.28万元，前三季度扣非利润几乎全部来自上半年。第三季度贡献了约35%的累计营收，却仅贡献约1%的累计扣非净利润，收入与利润的贡献明显不匹配。 因此，华谊集团这份三季报呈现出两种不同的变化，与去年同期相比，第三季度收入增长、扣非扭亏，盈利有所修复；放在今年前三季度内部看，当季扣非利润贡献却明显偏低。 净利润增长逾13倍是最醒目的数字，而后续业绩能否持续改善，更取决于增长的收入能否转化为更高的扣非利润。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 意外！79%企业GPU利用率竟不足一半
articles.summary: AI 军备竞赛打到现在，场面似乎开始变得魔幻…… 近日，科技媒体 VentureBeat 旗下研究机构 VentureBeat Intelligence 汇集的 2026 年第三季度连续调研数据显示， 79% 的企业受访者表示，其 GPU 算力至少有一半时间处于完全闲置状态。 这一数据在三个月中始终稳定维持在 77% 至 81% 的高位 。换句话说，在这批受访企业中，GPU 使用不充分已经成为一个持续存在的现象。 但更令人匪夷所思的是， 在这批 GPU 平均利用率不超过 50% 的企业里，70% 的公司仍计划在未来 12 个月内引入、扩充或更换新的 AI 计算平台。 VentureBeat 旗下研究机构 VentureBeat Intelligence 汇总了其在 2026 年 7 月、8 月和 9 月开展的三轮人工智能基础设施与算力领域 VB Pulse 调查结果。三轮调查共吸引了 385 名符合条件的受访者，他们来自员工人数不少于 100 人的机构，其中也包括代表其主要客户作答的咨询顾问。 一边是硬件在机房吃灰，一边是 AI 预算账单仍在加速狂飙，问题已然浮出水面：现有资源尚未充分利用，企业为什么还要继续寻找新的 AI 平台？ 再看投资回报。VentureBeat 今年 9 月的调查显示，在 64 名计划采用新 AI 平台的受访者中，58 人没有经过财务部门审核的投资回报率（ROI）数据，占比高达 91%。 这意味着， 相当一部分受访企业在准备下一轮 AI 投入时，尚未形成经过财务审核的收益测算。 当然，没有经过审核的 ROI，不等于项目没有收益。同一调查中，没有新平台采用计划的受访者也普遍缺少这类数据，但它至少表明，企业 AI 投资的财务评估，可能还没有跟上基础设施投入的速度。也就是说，AI 能力正在快速进入生产环境，但到底花了多少钱、创造了多少价值，仍是许多企业没有完全回答的问题。 这些数字之所以重要，是因为华尔街正在激烈争论 AI 是否已经形成泡沫，而 VentureBeat 基于调查提出了一个颇具争议的判断：AI 泡沫的风险，可能已经出现在企业内部…… 错位的两套账单：闲置的「算力」与烧钱的「API」 表面上看，这种「一边闲置、一边加码」的现象极度违背商业常理，尤其是在多数技术负责人正面临削减 AI 预算压力的当下：一些技术负责人告诉 VentureBeat，在今年秋季的预算季，他们正承受着削减 AI 账单的巨大压力。 但深入企业内部架构会发现，企业的真实 AI 需求并没有消失，而是精准地落在了现有硬件根本承接不住的地方。 专业人士和消费者正在使用越来越多的 AI，而其中大量工作依赖 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 提供的前沿模型，这种需求将在未来一段时间内继续支撑这些公司在算力方面的投入。 真正的错配发生在更下游的企业内部：企业当前正同时为两类截然不同的 AI 支出买单，而这两者之间存在无法逾越的鸿沟： 恐慌驱动的算力储备： 前两年全球算力短缺的焦虑下，大量企业出于「防踏空」心理提前锁定并采购了 GPU 集群。然而，硬件到位后，企业却缺乏成熟的内部场景与工程能力将其跑满。 对闭源前沿模型的路径依赖：业务团队与工程师更倾向于直接调用 OpenAI、Anthropic 和 Google 旗下最顶尖的闭源前沿模型。企业通过这些公司的 API 按 Token 付费，或者通过月度订阅、大型云服务商购买模型能力，无法将其直接部署到自己此前掌控的本地或托管 GPU 上。 这就造成了一个极为讽刺的局面：自建算力成了沉没资产，而调取闭源 API 的成本却以惊人速度吞噬预算。 今年 8 月的时候，《财富》杂志就曾报道过，Uber 首席技术官透露，由于公司鼓励员工尽可能多地使用 AI 工具，甚至专门设立了「排行榜」，根据软件工程师使用这些工具的情况进行排名。 结果就是，几个月内便耗尽了 2026 全年的 AI 预算，企业不得不宣告「Token 狂欢（Tokenmaxxing）」时代的终结。 调研数据进一步佐证了这种结构性割裂：在计划采购新计算平台且 GPU 闲置的企业中，90% 将目光投向了公有云与模型 API 服务商，仅有 8% 考虑扩建本地私有集群。与此同时，91% 计划引入新平台的企业，根本拿不出任何一份经过财务部门审核过的实际 ROI 评估。 当然，一部分算力闲置可能是企业有意为之，比如为了应对需求高峰而预留 GPU 资源，而计划引入的新平台也可能用于替换旧平台。 从「算力军备竞赛」转向「推理经济学」 如果说 GPU 闲置暴露的是基础设施利用效率问题，那么 Agent 的普及，则可能让企业面临更加复杂的成本挑战。 VentureBeat 预计，接下来企业 AI 支出中用于模型调用的比例将越来越高。尤其是伴随业务从简单的生成式对话迈向多步骤自主的 AI Agent，企业的算力矛盾正在被进一步放大。 Gartner 预测，到 2028 年，单个 Agent 工作流的推理成本将上升 5 倍以上。 这并不意味着模型的 Token 单价会越来越贵，事实上，随着推理基础设施和模型效率持续优化，单位 Token 价格可能继续下降，但真正的问题是，Agent 完成任务时消耗的 Token 数量，可能增长得比单价下降更快。 其中一个很容易被忽视的成本来源，就是上下文。以 AI 编程为例，模型不仅需要理解当前问题，还需要不断读取项目代码、系统指令和历史执行记录，随着任务推进，这些上下文可能在多次请求中重复出现。如果每次都重新处理，成本会迅速累积，这也是上下文缓存越来越受到重视的原因。 NVIDIA 工程师在一份技术指南中提到，在其研究的 Claude Code 会话场景中，首次调用之后，后续请求约 85% 至 97% 的上下文可以通过缓存复用，而 Anthropic 的缓存读取价格，根据模型和定价条件，可以低至普通输入 Token 价格的四十分之一至十分之一。 对于需要持续执行任务的 Agent 来说，这种优化可能带来相当可观的节省。 另一个变量，则是 Agent 数量。行业评测机构 Vals AI 的一项编程任务测试发现，采用主 Agent 调度多个子 Agent 的方案，成本达到单 Agent 的 1.8 至 5.1 倍。 然而，在四种测试配置中，只有一种取得了统计显著的性能提升。换句话说，增加 Agent 可能带来更强的能力，也可能只是让更多模型同时消耗 Token。 告别粗放扩张：企业务实自救的路径 面对极高的闲置率与失控的模型调用账单，对于企业来说，或许粗放式的「盲目采购」正在成为过去。业内普遍认为，在企业签署下一份算力合同之前，应当优先在既有资产中挤出效率：想办法利用已经付费购买的算力和 Token，完成更多实际工作。 具体来说，需要做好以下几件事情： 衡量每项已完成任务的成本，同时考虑 GPU 算力资源和 API 调用支出； 测试不同模型和推理强度，确定企业的默认配置：评价标准应当是每项已完成任务的成本，而非单个 Token 的价格。因为便宜的模型可能消耗更多 Token，最终导致每项任务的成本反而更高； 只向 Agent 提供它实际需要的上下文，并缓存重复使用的内容： 无论通过模型供应商 API，还是在企业自有基础设施上运行，都应当如此； 只有当任务能够拆分为可并行执行的部分时，才增加第二个 Agent； 将常规、高频任务从前沿模型 API 迁移到运行在闲置算力上的开放模型， 例如分类、信息抽取和文本摘要； 利用剩余的 GPU 闲置时间处理可以延后执行的任务，例如批量推理、模型评测和微调。 最终的目标，是让企业为每一项实际完成的工作，支付更合理的成本。 这也让开篇那组令人惊讶的数据有了新的意义，79% 的 GPU 低利用率，与 70% 的新平台采用意愿，并不能直接证明 AI 泡沫已经形成，更不能说明整个 AI 行业正在走向产能过剩。但它提醒企业： 资源投入与实际需求之间，确实可能存在需要重新审视的落差。 过去几年，AI 行业习惯用参数规模、训练算力和资本开支衡量进展。随着技术逐渐进入真实业务，这些指标之外，还需要一套更加务实的评价体系：企业究竟用 AI 完成了多少工作？成功率有多高？节省了多少时间？又付出了多少成本？ 对于模型厂商来说，这意味着竞争将不只围绕模型能力展开，还会延伸到推理效率、部署灵活性与整体任务成本。对于企业来说，比继续囤积算力更重要的，可能是先想办法把已经拥有的 GPU 和 Token 用好。 毕竟，GPU 买来是为了干活的，真正值得关注的，是它最终创造了多少价值…… 本文来源： 机器之心 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 韩国7900名富豪净卖三星海力士1483亿韩元，转买杠杆芯片ETF
articles.summary: 韩国高净值投资者正在重构其半导体仓位——从直接持有龙头个股转向杠杆化ETF产品，这一结构性切换折射出该群体对芯片板块短期波动的审慎态度，以及对更广泛市场反弹的定向押注。 据首尔经济日报委托一家大型券商对约7900名高净值投资者（金融资产超过30亿韩元，约合210万美元）的持仓进行分析， 10月1日至20日期间，该群体对三星电子和SK海力士的净卖出额分别达到55.9亿韩元和92.4亿韩元，合计约148.3亿韩元。 与此同时， KODEX半导体杠杆ETF以332亿韩元的净买入额跃居本月最大净买入标的。 这一切换信号对两只芯片巨头的股价构成潜在压力。高净值群体的持续减持意味着大盘权重股面临来自"聪明钱"的系统性抛压，而资金向杠杆产品的集中流入，也引发市场对ETF溢价及流动性风险的关注。 从个股到ETF：高净值资金的结构性切换 本月高净值投资者买入榜前五名中，有三席被ETF占据，与上月形成鲜明对比——9月榜单清一色为个股，包括三星电子优先股（净买入59.6亿韩元）、三星电机（19.9亿韩元）、三星SDI（11.7亿韩元）、斗山能源（8.2亿韩元）及斗山燃料电池（7.7亿韩元）。 分析人士将这一转变解读为： 投资者选择通过ETF押注板块整体上涨，而非对单一大盘股进行直接下注。 一家大型券商官员表示，本月高净值投资者的核心特征是在降低对大盘芯片股直接敞口的同时，仍维持对板块及整体市场上行的方向性判断。 这种操作逻辑在一定程度上反映出该群体对三星电子、SK海力士个股基本面的分歧或谨慎——在连续两个月净卖出两只股票的背景下，他们并未选择离场观望，而是通过杠杆ETF保留了对半导体板块的敞口，实质上是以更高的波动率换取对个股风险的规避。 杠杆ETF领跑，看多情绪主导方向 KODEX半导体杠杆ETF追踪半导体指数日涨幅的两倍，属于高风险产品，以332亿韩元的净买入额位居本月榜首。与此同时，追踪KOSPI 200指数日涨幅两倍的KODEX杠杆ETF获净买入225亿韩元，KODEX 200则获净买入105亿韩元。 与看多仓位扩张形成对照的是，高净值投资者本月净卖出80亿韩元的KODEX 200期货反向2X——该产品在指数下跌时获益。 这意味着该群体在指数联动产品上同步削减空头、加码多头，整体方向性判断偏向市场中期走强。 在个股层面，本月仅有SK Square（净买入28.6亿韩元）和三星SDI（净买入12.5亿韩元）获得净流入，其余大盘芯片股均遭减持，进一步印证了资金从个股向ETF迁移的主线逻辑。 杠杆ETF偏好背后的风险积聚 韩国散户及高净值投资者对杠杆ETF的偏好由来已久，这类产品因其高弹性特征在市场波动加剧时往往吸引大量资金涌入。然而，杠杆ETF的结构性特点决定了其风险不可忽视： 每日复利机制在震荡市中会产生显著的路径损耗，而集中买入还可能推高ETF相对于净值的溢价，加大踩踏风险。 当前芯片ETF资金流入的可持续性同样存疑。高净值投资者选择杠杆产品，本质上是对短期板块反弹的博弈，而非基于个股基本面的长期配置。一旦半导体板块出现超预期调整，杠杆ETF持有者面临的损失将成倍放大，且集中持仓可能加速抛售踩踏。 对三星电子和SK海力士而言，高净值群体的持续净卖出构成不可忽视的边际压力。尽管这一群体的绝对卖出规模相对于两只股票的日均成交量有限，但其行为往往具有风向标意义，可能影响更广泛市场参与者的情绪与操作。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 马斯克预警：200多家AI云厂商面临清洗，Nebius、CoreWeave盘前跌超4%
articles.summary: 马斯克一番"行业洗牌"警告，令本已承压的Neocloud板块再遭重挫。 周一盘前，Nebius、CoreWeave和Iren股价均一度跌逾4%，此后跌幅有所收窄，目前在2%至3%区间内波动。导火索是马斯克周日在X平台发文， 直言200多家Neocloud公司将面临"小鱼级别的死亡与整合"。 这一表态令市场对该板块债务驱动式扩张能否持续的疑虑进一步加深。 过去一个月，Neocloud板块已遭受重创——CoreWeave和Nebius累计跌幅均超30%，Iren更暴跌逾40%。此轮抛售始于本月早些时候CoreWeave五年期信用违约互换利差攀升至通常被视为财务困境信号的水平，其债券收益率亦同步走高，令投资者对该行业大规模举债购买英伟达芯片、建设数据中心的商业模式产生严重质疑。 马斯克发出行业洗牌警告 马斯克在X平台的帖子中写道："过去几周，债务市场几乎已对所有在AI数据中心之外缺乏实质性营收的公司关闭了融资渠道。"他随即补充： "这意味着200多家Neocloud将迎来小鱼级别的死亡与整合。部分公司能够存活，但不会太多。" 马斯克此番发言，是在回应Social Capital创始人Chamath Palihapitiya的一篇帖子。 Palihapitiya在文中指出，与当前预测相比，2027年将出现"大量部分闲置算力和库存中积压的算力"，这些资产"已被购置并付款，但实际回报低于资本总成本，或正在蒙尘"。他还表示， "2027年将是动荡之年，将淘汰一批错误和糟糕的押注，同时也将是少数玩家的整合之年"。 值得注意的是，马斯克旗下SpaceX自身运营数据中心并对外出售算力，与Neocloud公司存在直接竞争关系。 英伟达与各家Neocloud为需求背书 面对市场恐慌，英伟达上周在德国柏林举办的GTC活动上出手为该板块站台。英伟达CEO 黄仁勋在接受CNBC采访时表示，市场对Neocloud的需求"爆表"。 "目前缺失的是支撑增长的营运资本……因为AI各个领域的需求实在太旺盛，资本供给出现了稀缺，"黄仁勋说， "资本需求远大于资本供给，但这个问题终将得到解决。 "英伟达是多家Neocloud公司的投资方。 Nebius首席营收官Marc Boroditsky则试图将公司与CoreWeave的困境切割，他在接受CNBC采访时表示，"我们没有背负那样的债务规模"，并称若公司将2027年的算力如期上线，将会全部售罄，2028年或将出现"同样的供不应求局面"。 Iren联席CEO Daniel Roberts同样为需求前景辩护。"我们理解投资者关注度的上升，但当我们与客户沟通时，什么都没有改变，需求依然在，"Roberts上周告诉CNBC，"明年，我们正在与客户洽谈的容量已是我们可能上线规模的数倍，而且最近一个月，2028年的需求也开始进入视野。" 债务压力成板块核心隐忧 投资者的核心担忧在于，Neocloud公司大量举债购买昂贵的英伟达芯片并建设数据中心，其商业模式能否在资本市场收紧的环境下持续运转。马斯克的警告恰恰戳中了这一软肋——一旦债务市场对缺乏独立营收的公司关闭融资渠道，依赖外部资本滚动扩张的Neocloud将面临生存危机。 CoreWeave信用违约互换利差的异动已率先释放出市场的不安情绪，并引发了过去一个月的持续抛售。尽管英伟达和各家Neocloud高管均强调需求端并无问题，但供给侧的资本约束正成为悬在整个行业头顶的达摩克利斯之剑。市场目前的分歧在于：需求的真实性能否最终转化为足以覆盖高额债务成本的现金流，而这一答案或许要等到2027年才能揭晓。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 九号公司前三季度营收增长近两成，成本与费用上升冲击盈利
articles.summary: 九号公司的收入规模继续扩大，成本与费用的上升也对盈利提出了更高要求。 10月26日，九号公司发布2026年第三季度报告。前三季度，公司实现营业收入219.43亿元，同比增长19.32%；归母净利润13.51亿元，同比下降24.40%；扣非净利润12.15亿元，同比下降32.43%。 其中，第三季度实现营业收入75.85亿元，同比增长14.10%；归母净利润3.43亿元，同比下降37.18%；扣非净利润2.47亿元，同比下降49.21%。 对于利润下降，九号公司表示，主要受汇兑损失、原材料价格上涨及研发等期间费用增加影响。收入保持增长，但多项成本和支出增加，使公司当期盈利承压。 收入端仍是这份财报中的积极因素。 按披露数据估算，九号公司前三季度营收较去年同期增加约35.53亿元，其中第三季度增加约9.37亿元。公司在已有规模上继续实现两位数增长，为研发投入和后续业务发展提供了支撑。 不过，第三季度的收入增速低于前三季度累计水平，利润降幅则更大。对九号公司而言，当前需要解决的问题，是如何让业务规模的扩大更充分地体现到利润上。 利润率的变化直观反映了这一点。按归母净利润与营业收入的比例计算，前三季度归母净利率约为6.16%；第三季度为4.52%，去年同期约为8.21%。也就是说，同样实现100元收入，第三季度对应的归母净利润由去年约8.2元降至约4.5元。 影响利润的几项因素中，原材料涨价直接增加生产成本。营收增长能带来更多收入，但最终能留下多少利润，还取决于采购成本、生产效率及产品结构。在原材料价格上涨的情况下，新增收入带来的收益需要先消化一部分成本压力。 汇兑损失则增加了盈利的波动。九号公司此前公告显示，公司存在境外销售，主要采用美元、欧元等币种结算，汇率变化会影响经营业绩，公司也已安排开展外汇套期保值业务。因此，观察当期利润，需要同时考虑产品经营表现和汇率变化的影响。 研发等期间费用增加，则反映了当期盈利与持续投入之间的平衡。研发支出会影响本期利润，也可能为后续产品迭代和业务增长提供支持。这部分投入的效果，最终要通过产品销售和盈利贡献来体现。 从累计利润构成看，前三季度扣非净利润12.15亿元，占归母净利润的比重约90%。尽管同比有所下降，公司前三季度盈利仍主要由扣除非经常性损益后的利润构成。 第三季度，归母净利润与扣非净利润之间相差9600万元，非经常性损益对当季盈利形成了一定支撑。扣非净利润降幅达到49.21%，也说明当季盈利面临的压力较为明显，后续仍需关注修复情况。 整体来看，九号公司前三季度保持了收入增长，并实现13.51亿元归母净利润，但成本、汇率和费用变化削弱了收入增长对盈利的带动作用。 接下来，公司业绩的看点将同时落在增长和效率上，一方面是收入能否保持扩张，另一方面是成本控制及研发投入能否带来更好的利润贡献。随着业务规模扩大，如何提高每一元收入的盈利能力，将成为九号公司下一阶段的重要课题。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
